original_title: Documents not showing on the docket
polished_title: Documents have not appeared on the docket
original_text:
Unfortunately, we are not the party responsible for uploading filed information to the docket.
This is an action completed by the Clerk of the Courts system.
The e-filing portal sends the documents you upload to the clerk.
The clerk then processed through their case management system, then dockets the forms you submitted to the docket.
Please contact the Clerk of the Courts office in the county the case is filed in to ask
if something is wrong with the docket or prohibiting documents from showing on the case.
polished_text:
The E-Filing Portal transmits submitted documents to the applicable Clerk of Court. The Clerk then processes the filing through its case-management system and controls when documents appear on the official docket.

If the Portal shows that the filing was accepted but the documents are not on the docket, contact the Clerk in the county where the case is filed and ask about the docket status.

original_title: Can I file my case on the website?
polished_title: Can this matter be filed through the Portal?
original_text:
Thank you for contacting the MyFLCourtAccess.com website Help Desk.
Support for the website MyFLCourtAccess.com is limited to only providing navigational & technical guidance for the purpose of filing documentation that you have ready to file to create a case, or file to an existing case.
For any questions outside of navigating the website to file documentation, please contact your Clerk of the Courts office.
Please be advised that the E-Filing portal website MyFLCourtAccess.com is not the Clerk of the Court or the District Court of Appeals.
Instructions are not exact, and we are unable to tell you exactly which drop downs or forms are needed to file, as we are limited by legal restrictions and cannot offer legal advice.
1. What type of case are you filing?
a. Circuit Civil
b. County Civil (Small Claims under $8,000) (types less than $50,000) (Eviction)
c. Domestic Relation/Family
d. Probate
e. Juvenile Dependency
f. Adoption
g. Domestic Violence / Stalking / Cyber Bullying
2. What County are you filing in?
Some counties will have different requirements, procedures, and forms.
3. What forms are needed?
Please visit the Clerk of the Court’s website for the county you are filing your case in for information on procedures, forms that are required to be filed, and to determine the Division, Case Type, and Sub Type you will need to file under.
Most cases in Circuit or County Civil courts will require a “Complaint” or “Statement of Claim” form.
Most cases in Family/Domestic Relations, a Petition is to be the first document you upload, followed by others that may be required.
Probate: varies. Check with the Clerk's website to determine what is needed.
Once you have the forms needed to file, you can use the below for guidance.
El servicio de asistencia del portal de presentación electrónica, support@myflcourtaccess.com, solo ofrece asistencia técnica y de navegación para el sitio web MyFLCourtAccess.com
para el envío (carga) de la documentación que esté listo para presentar para crear un caso o para un caso existente.
No proporcionamos información sobre el procedimiento del caso, ni podemos asesorarlo, ni proporcionamos los formularios necesarios para presentar ni dónde encontrarlos.

New Attorney to case/ PHV / NOT showing up in My Cases
An attorney will not be able to access or view any case dockets on the Florida Courts E-Filing portal that they are not the Attorney of Record for AND if they have not filed electronically to the case through the website.

If you are a Pro Hac Vice attorney, being admitted to the case does not automatically allow you to access the case docket through the e-filing portal.
If you are not going to be the attorney of record, and you are not filing to the case, please contact the Florida attorney you are working with and ask for them to add you to the service list on the next filing.
When filings are done after that point, and the filer checks your box (it is up to the filer to decide whether to check you for service because it is not done automatically to everyone on the service list) you will get an email with a copy of what has been filed to that case.
Warning, if you leave the email untouched, or it ends up in your spam for more than 14 days, you can no longer access the documents from the email. We usually tell eService recipients to open and download the filings immediately so that doesn't happen.

polished_title: Proposed document remains in Transmitted status
original_text:
The filing is still in the transmitted status.
On filings "transmitted" to the Judge:
Please call the JA with the filing number (9-digits) to see if they call pull it from the Judicial Circuit Interface queue.
Here is how proposed orders are supposed to move through the system:
Filing is submitted.
Then transmitted to the Judicial Circuit Interface.
The judge's office goes in and pulls the filing from the judicial circuit interface.
The judge signs off or denies the proposed order.
The Judge's office sends the denied or signed filing to the Clerk. (at the Judge's discretion what the exact procedure is, it may or may not go through the clerk)
The Clerk files to the docket if approved and signed.
Or the judge’s office files directly to the docket.
If the Judge's office cannot find the filing, they may require you to refile.
Also, The Clerk does not always file the signed copy, nor does the judge always send the signed or rejections through the e-portal system. This means you will need to check the docket to make sure signed orders are not being missed. The Clerk of the Court’s have their own procedures in which they send out the signed orders if the Judge’s office does not process. You may want to call and check with the Clerk and or the JA on what their procedure is.
polished_text:
A proposed document in Transmitted status has been sent to the judicial interface but has not completed the judge/Clerk process.

Contact the Judicial Assistant with the nine-digit filing number and ask whether the filing is available in the Judicial Circuit Interface queue. The judge's office and Clerk control what happens after transmission, including approval, denial, docketing, or a request to refile.

Check the official docket and follow the current instructions from the Judicial Assistant or Clerk. Do not refile solely because the Portal still shows Transmitted unless the appropriate office directs you to do so.

County Changes:

County transfer

Information in your corrections filing disappearing.
Uploading: will upload a different PDF file than what you chose
Inability to make payments
Inability to submit the filing
May check the box for emergency filing
Slowness on the website
Sign Out using the Sign Out hyperlink, and sign back in.
Signing Out should be done:
a. Every time you leave the website.
b. After 15-20 minutes of being idle.
If not, it can cause issues with functions on the website.
Have you checked the formatting of your electronic file: No color, has to be unlocked/unsecured, no zipped / compressed files.
Instead of using a saved link, hand key the website into the URL address bar on the web browser.
1. Clear your web browser cache / cookies and update the browser at least every 2 weeks.
2. Make sure in your web browser settings, you list our website the allowance for pop ups and redirects.
3. Verify with your IT Department that the following websites are allowed access through your firewall as 1 or 2 of the sites needed are coming out of the Netherlands:
https://checkoutshopper-live.adyen.com and *.myflcourtaccess.com, *.vimeocdn.com, *.vimeo.com, *.jsdelivr.net, and *.typekit.net.
If you are trying to file to a case:  Start your filing over from the beginning.
Do NOT pull and resume any submission from the workbench.
If the above does not work, try a different web browser or from a different computer to see if your results are any different.
Restart your machine after the troubleshooting steps have been used.
I cannot guarantee this will fix the issue, but they are the steps that we ask you to apply first.

original_title: Symptoms associated with an improper sign-out
polished_title: Symptoms that may indicate a stale Portal session
original_text:
As insignificant as the Sign Out instructions may seem, if you do not use them, you may experience issues with:
Information in your corrections filing disappearing.
Uploading: will upload a different PDF file than what you chose
Inability to make payments
Inability to submit the filing
May check the box for emergency filing
Slowness on the website
polished_text:
A stale or improperly closed Portal session may contribute to symptoms such as:

• Information disappearing from a Correction Queue filing
• A different PDF appearing from the file selected
• Payment or submission failures
• Unexpected emergency-filing selection
• General slowness or inconsistent page behavior

Treat these as possible session symptoms, not proof of the cause.

original_title: Sign out and sign back in
polished_title: Sign out correctly and start a new session
original_text:
Sign Out using the Sign Out hyperlink, and sign back in.
Signing Out should be done:
a. Every time you leave the website.
b. After 15-20 minutes of being idle.
If not, it can cause issues with functions on the website.
polished_text:
Select the Sign Out link in the upper-right area of the Portal, close the browser, reopen it, and sign in again.

Use Sign Out whenever you leave the Portal and after an idle timeout. Closing the browser window without signing out may leave an incomplete session.

original_text: Have you checked the formatting of your electronic file: No color, has to be unlocked/unsecured, no zipped / compressed files.

• PDF or PDF/A format, as applicable
• Unlocked, unsecured, and not password protected
• Not compressed or contained in a ZIP file
• Required page size and file-size limits
• No prohibited color content
• Compatible filename and characters

I cannot guarantee this will fix the issue, but they are the steps that we ask you to apply first.

polished_title: Complete document-upload checklist
original_text:
We also provide the following steps to provide you with a better filing environment.
I am going to list the below information, highlighting on some points I feel are important.
I know you may have tried of the items on here, but because I have only had 2 people report something similar to this issue, and it's not widespread,
I am limited on what assistance I can offer.
On uploading, the formatting and the names of the files are crucial:
Please adhere to the information below when filing.
You cannot use the Safari web browser that is on most Apple/Mac devices.
Your file must be in PDF or PDF/a format.
If you are scanning pages into a PDF, make sure they are at 300DPI
*Will NOT accept compressed or zipped files.
*Will NOT accept PDF files if the file name has special or odd characters
In naming your PDF file:
Do NOT use hyphens, underscores, or odd characters (%^&*( )=+) or web dings
*Will NOT accept PDF files if the file name exceeds 36 characters in length.
*Will not accept “locked” or “Secured” PDF files.
***NO VIDEOS*** Please call the clerk of the court in the county your case is filed in and ask how to get that submitted to them
**NO COLOR PICTURES** If they must be in color, call the clerk to ask how to submit them outside of the portal.
No document in color other than black, including the signatures will be accepted.
The page size cannot exceed 8.5 x 11
DO NOT SAVE TO THE WORKBENCH TO GO BACK LATER TO RESUME.
IT WILL NOT WORK.
When uploading documents: make sure the 100% bar changes to a decimal number. If it does not, you cannot upload other documents.
polished_text:
Before uploading, verify each item below:

1. Use a desktop or laptop and a currently approved browser.
2. Save the document as PDF or PDF/A, as required for the document type.
3. For scanned documents, use 300 DPI unless current guidance specifies otherwise.
4. Do not upload compressed or ZIP files.
5. Remove incompatible filename characters. The manager source specifically identifies punctuation and special characters as possible causes.
6. Keep the filename within the current approved character limit. The supplied manager source states 36 characters, including spaces; confirm before sending.
7. Remove document security, encryption, password protection, and locked settings.
8. Confirm that the page size is Letter: 8.5 × 11 inches.
9. Confirm the current requirements for color content, photographs, audio, and video. The supplied manager guidance does not permit video or audio uploads and directs color-submission questions to the Clerk.
10. Wait for each upload to finish processing before adding another document.
11. Do not save a failed filing to Workbench and return later. Start over after completing the applicable troubleshooting.

If a document must be submitted in a format the Portal does not accept, contact the applicable Clerk of Court for an approved alternate method.

original_title: Yahoo, Gmail, AOL, and DMARC/DKIM reply

original_text:
Yahoo, Gmail, and AOL users:
If you run into a DMARC/DKIM issue, we are unable to correct this for you.

4. Confirm whether the message appears in the Portal Email Log.

The source includes a 2024 Proofpoint article for background. Treat it as reference material only and confirm the current approved guidance before sending.

polished_title: PDF formatting, conversion, and upload review
original_text:
Loss of information when filing Indexes, Exhibit markers, Bookmarks, Page Numbers, etc.
* Portal isn’t accepting the PDF files you are trying to upload.
If this contains the following, your file will need to be in PDF/a format (see attached document):
Transcripts & Briefs
Contains bookmarks or indexing
We typically see these issues due to the way the files are being created or formatted.
1. Using embedded fonts not recognized by the system.
2. Not leaving the space needed in the margin area.
3. The type of software / program being used for your conversion.
When filing the type of files that have Headers / Footers, Page Numbering, etc., the PDF file is to be formatted / converted in a specific way.
Margins and Print Area: It’s very important to stay within the guidelines, or the header/footers and page numbers will disappear as well as other information.
**Transcripts with any indexing, bookmarks etc, MUST be in PDF/A 2-B format.
PDF files shall be filed in a format capable of being electronically searched and printed.
Unfortunately, we cannot correct or convert your files for you.
I am listing some information below, as well as attaching the PDF FAQs to assist in helping you determine if there is a formatting issue you will need to resolve.
1. No locked, secured or encrypted PDF files
2. Do not scan in pages using a DPI larger than 300.
3. The name you have given the file is incompatible.
If your file has special characters you will need to rename the electronic file.
Example:
if it looks like asd_812#.pdf, rename it, removing the unacceptable characters to something else like asd812.pdf
4. The name of your PDF file cannot exceed 36 characters including blank spaces.
5. The file was corrupted in transition from the original format to the format you currently have. Ex: Word to pdf or jpg to .docx
6. The file page size is too large. instead of 8.5x11 it is 8.62x11.26 or any other size other than letter. (may need to check your software to undo any automatic settings that may be converting them a specific way other than what you require)
7. Do NOT upload compressed or zipped files.
8. When uploading a file, make sure it is completely uploaded before trying to add another document. (the 100% green bar needs to be gone and reflect a percentage number)
9. Information entered is either incorrect or missed
10. Remove ALL COLOR- the portal does not accept any color documentation including signatures, hyperlinks and email addresses.
11. The maximum upload at one time, with all files combined cannot exceed 50mb for Lower Courts or 200mb for Supreme and Appellate Courts.
That means if you upload 4 documents and their combined size exceeds the maximum; your files will not upload.
12. Formatting is not correct. ie: embedded fonts, margin errors, etc.
13. ***NO VIDEOS / NO COLOR PICTURES, NO AUDIO RECORDINGS***
polished_text:
Use this checklist when a PDF is rejected, displays missing or stacked text, loses bookmarks or page numbers, or changes after upload:

1. Confirm whether the document must be PDF/A. The source specifically identifies transcripts, briefs, bookmarks, and indexing as common PDF/A cases.
2. Use a reputable PDF creator and standard fonts. Embedded or unsupported fonts can alter text.
3. Confirm the page margins and printable area. Headers, footers, page numbers, and exhibit markers can disappear when they fall outside the supported area.
4. Remove password protection, encryption, security, and locked settings.
5. Use no more than 300 DPI for scanned pages unless current guidance specifies otherwise.
6. Rename the file using a simple filename without special characters.
7. Keep the filename within the current approved limit. The source states 36 characters, including spaces.
8. Confirm that every page is exactly 8.5 × 11 inches.
9. Do not upload compressed or ZIP files.
10. Wait for each file to finish processing before adding another.
11. Confirm the current color, audio, video, and combined-upload limits. The source lists 50 MB for lower courts and 200 MB for Supreme/Appellate Courts; verify current limits before sending.
12. If the original document and the Portal result differ, preserve the original and escalate with the test result under the current procedure.

Portal Support cannot repair or convert a customer's document. Provide approved guidance and document the result of each check.

Confirm:

• Whether any payment is still pending or processing

• Whether the payment method can be removed after those items complete

polished_title: Filing is stuck and cannot be completed
original_text:
When you get "stuck" like that, it means you must start over.
Make sure the Petition is the first form you upload in the documents area.
Do not try to pull the saved submission from the workbench.
You will need to make sure not to leave your computer until the filing has been done.
If you leave the site open more than 15 minutes, it times out, which could cause issues.
Make sure when you are done with the website that you are using the Sign Out hyperlink in the
upper right corner to log out. If not, it could also cause issues with function when you go back into the site.
polished_text:
When the filing becomes stuck:

1. Stop using the current filing session.
2. Complete the clean-session browser troubleshooting.
3. Start the filing again from the beginning; do not resume the failed Workbench submission.
4. Upload the required initiating document first when the case workflow requires it.
5. Complete the filing without leaving the Portal idle. The source identifies 15–20 minutes as a possible timeout range; confirm current behavior.
6. Use the Sign Out link when leaving the Portal.

Record the page where the filing became stuck and whether the new session changed the result.

When this happens, it means there was a function issue.

original_title: When trying to resubmit a filing that was in the Correction Queue- but Payment wont process

original_text:
The payment you made previously has been refunded.
Go back through the filing, starting with the case information area. Make sure all the drop downs are correct. Scroll to the bottom and click next.
On your case parties, click the edit link. On the drop down next to role:
for the Plaintiff, check mark both boxes: Primary Party & Filed on Behalf of- make sure all the information is correct, (check that zip code is there) click save.

NO hyphens or underscores, no odd characters (%^&*( )=+) or web dings

If this does not work, please use the following troubleshooting information to relay to you IT Department.
(Also send them the web browser troubleshooting steps)
If still unable to get your payment to process: please email: [internal staff email redacted] referencing ticket #
polished_text:
Before escalating a Correction Queue payment failure:

1. Confirm the status of the original payment or refund in TPE.
2. Reopen the filing from the beginning of the Correction Queue workflow and review every case-information field.
3. Edit each case party and confirm the required role selections, address, and ZIP code, then save.

7. Complete the browser, session, pop-up, and firewall troubleshooting.
8. Record the exact error and result of each step.

original_title: How do I get a PDF out of XFA format?
polished_title: Convert an XFA form to a standard PDF
original_text: How do I convert an XFA to PDF? To convert XFA PDF to normal PDF, click the Print button, on the Print window that opens, tick Print as Image, and click Print. The XFA form will be converted to a PDF file that you can open with any PDF reader.
polished_text:
An XFA form may need to be flattened before the Portal can process it.

Using an approved PDF application:
1. Open Print.
2. Select an approved Print to PDF destination.
3. If available, enable Print as Image.
4. Create the new PDF.
5. Open the new file and verify every page, field, signature, and attachment before uploading.

original_title: When documents change while viewing / correcting in the documents area
polished_title: Documents change while viewing or correcting a filing
original_text:
This can sometimes happen for a couple of reasons.
1. Your web browser needs to have the cache and cookies cleared and the browser updated.
2. You did not sign out of the website using the Sign Out hyperlink but just X out of the web page, which can cause function issues when you log back in
over an already "open" session.
3. The website was open too long causing it to time out. Usually, if you have the website open and idle for more than 15-20 minutes.
4. Not going through the process of choosing a document type before uploading the new document to replace the one during a filing in the correction queue.
If the above happens while fixing a filing in the correction queue to an existing case:
Please go to the docket, open the documents to see what has been filed, then upload documents that were not uploaded in another filing to the
existing case.
Party Names from the Financial ID#
You can look this up by going to My Submissions.
Enter the EPTL number from your statement: 4229336 into the Financial ID box.
Change the Submission date to a week before the money was removed from your account.
You can go back 90 days from todays date.
Click search.
It should bring up the filing for you to click on and see the case party names.
polished_text:
Possible causes include a stale browser session, an idle timeout, incomplete cache/cookie maintenance, or replacing a Correction Queue document without first selecting the correct document type.

1. Select Sign Out and close the browser.
2. Clear cache and cookies, update the browser, and start a new session.
3. Do not leave the filing idle for an extended period.
4. In Correction Queue, select the correct document type before uploading the replacement file.
5. Verify each preview before continuing.
6. If a required document was omitted from an accepted filing, review the official docket and submit the missing document as a separate filing only under the applicable Clerk and Portal procedure.
7. Preserve the original file and screenshots if the document changes again.

polished_title: PDF page size is larger than 8.5 × 11
original_text:
Depending on how you converted your pdf file, some printers and scanners used or the software program you are using to create the pdf, is not converting the document correctly.
When physically scanning, or printing pages out and then scanning:
Most machines have rollers (some plastic, some rubber). If they are worn down or need to be cleaned, they could be skewing the page when it pulls it through the machine. Then it throws it off the size you were scanning it to be.
Especially when the pages have been previously stapled or creased.
Or-
In the software or the setting on the machine itself:
You may need to review and or adjust the settings to the correct size.
There are a few websites that assist with the resizing / conversion of files.
If you would like to use it, see the attached flyer with instructions provided.
(note to HD person-attach the instructions to the email)
** Emailed the instructions on resizing documents for submission
polished_text:
A scanner, printer driver, or PDF-creation program may create pages that are slightly larger than Letter size.

1. Check every page, not only the first page.
2. Set the document or scanner output to Letter: 8.5 × 11 inches.
3. Disable automatic scaling, overscan, or custom paper-size settings.
4. Rescan pages that are skewed because of worn rollers, folds, staples, or creases.
5. Use the approved resizing instructions or approved local software.
6. Open the resized PDF and verify the content before upload.

Do not upload sensitive court documents to an unapproved public conversion website.

original_text:

Attached is what I converted to PDF/A but it gave me an error that certain components couldn’t convert.
That being said I was able to run the converted doc through the validation, and it passed the PDF/A check.

A file can pass a validator and still contain a visual conversion problem, so validation does not replace document review.

original_title: PDF file has corrupt. deleted, missing, or stacked verbiage
polished_title: Corrupted, missing, or stacked PDF text
original_text:
When you come across tickets where the filer is reporting their submitted PDF document had stuff deleted from it, letters turn into wingdings, letters stacked on top of one another it most likely is they are using a font that isn't standard. To test this, you will need to have them send you the original document and run it through the TEST Portal to see if the results are the same. If they are, you can post in Teams, provide the original document and tag Rao.
Recommendations for the filer (include the PDF/A FAQ document and the link to the video): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vwx288WZGaU
Make sure you are using a reputable PDF creator
Use one of the standard fonts: - Times Roman - Times Italic - Times Bold - Times Bold Italic - Courier Regular - Courier Oblique - Courier Bold - Courier Bold Oblique - Helvetica Regular - Helvetica Oblique - Helvetica Bold - Helvetica Bold Oblique - Symbol - ITC Zapf Dingbats
polished_text:
When text disappears, overlaps, or changes into symbols, unsupported or improperly embedded fonts may be the cause.

Analyst steps:
1. Obtain the original document through the approved secure process.
2. Reproduce the upload in the approved test environment.
3. Compare the original with the test result.
4. If the issue reproduces, preserve the original, screenshots, and test result and escalate under the current procedure.

Customer guidance:
• Use a reputable PDF creator.
• Use standard fonts when possible.
• Save or convert to the required PDF/A format.
• Review every page of the final PDF before uploading.

original_title: Unable to click on and preview the file they just uploaded:
polished_title: Uploaded PDF cannot be previewed
original_text:
May have had an update to their adobe or their web browser.
How to fix:
Go to your web browser setting- manage extensions- adobe and uncheck the (auto open)
then can preview the uploaded file the documents section.
polished_text:
A recent browser or Adobe extension update may change how PDFs open.

1. Confirm the browser and Adobe application are current.
2. Open the browser extension settings.
3. Review the Adobe PDF extension and disable automatic opening in the external application when the current browser procedure requires it.
4. Reload the Portal, upload the file again, and test Preview.
5. If the preview still fails, test another approved browser and record the result.

polished_title: Filename or 100-character-limit error
original_text:
The error is because of the way your PDF document is named.
Please try to keep it at a total of 36 spaces:
The name you have given the file is incompatible.
If your file has special characters (or exceeds more than 36 total spaces, including blanks) you will need to rename the electronic file.
Example:
if it looks like asd_812#.pdf, rename it, removing the unacceptable characters to something else like asd812.pdf
polished_text:
The error may be caused by an incompatible PDF filename.

1. Shorten the filename to the current approved limit. The manager source states 36 characters, including spaces.
2. Remove punctuation and special characters.
3. Use a simple letters-and-numbers filename.

Example: rename asd_812#.pdf to asd812.pdf.

Confirm the current filename limit before sending.
